title: Styling lists and tables
learningObjectives: Explain styling lists and tables and apply the layout behaviour correctly.

understand.concept: CSS can style list markers, spacing, borders, table cells, captions, and alternating rows. list-style-type and ::marker affect list markers; border-collapse and table layout properties influence table presentation.
understand.whyItMatters: Keep native list and table semantics. Visual styling should not remove useful structure, make headers hard to distinguish, or create poor contrast. Wide data tables may need a responsive wrapper that preserves access to all columns.
understand.analogy: A list is a set of related points and a table is a grid of related values; styling should make those relationships easier to scan.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; the browser uses formal formatting, containing-block, and painting rules.

explain.narrative: The list marker is coloured, and the table uses collapsed borders, padding, and alternating row backgrounds. Table headers remain semantic.

practise.guidedTask: Style a nested list and a small data table. Preserve captions and scope headers, and test the table on a narrow screen.
practise.independentTask: Build a small layout that demonstrates this behaviour. Test long content, keyboard navigation, and narrow viewports.
